headline: Poland has received the first batch of South Korean K2 Black Panther tanks under its latest $6.7 billion defense deal with Hyundai Rotem. Under the second contract, Poland is acquiring 180 K2 tanks. The first 28 vehicles have already been delivered and assigned to the 16th Pomeranian Mechanized Division. This brings Poland’s K2 fleet to 208 tanks. The new deliveries are part of Poland’s broader military rearmament program, launched following the outbreak of the war in Ukraine and focused on rapidly expanding the country’s fleet of modern armored vehicles. The first contract covered 180 K2GF tanks, all of which Poland received by the end of 2025. The second phase now focuses on gradually increasing the local production and integration of the K2 platform. Under the latest agreement, Poland will receive: • 116 K2GF tanks in 2026–2027; • 64 K2PL tanks in 2028–2030. The K2PL is tailored to the requirements of the Polish Army and features a greater share of domestic production. Of the 64 K2PLs, 61 are expected to be assembled in Poland at the Bumar-Łabędy plant in Gliwice using Polish components. The contract also includes a comprehensive support package comprising: • 25 K2-based armored engineering vehicles; • 25 armored bridge layers; • 31 repair and recovery vehicles; • ammunition; • personnel training; • technology transfer.

headline: Russia appears to be preparing for a renewed escalation in Ukraine as efforts to negotiate an end to the war have stalled, according to people familiar with discussions in Moscow cited by Bloomberg. The Kremlin is reportedly considering more intensive conventional ballistic missile strikes against Kyiv and infrastructure in other Ukrainian cities. Russian officials increasingly view Ukrainian attacks on refineries, logistics facilities and other targets inside Russia as attacks enabled by NATO support. The shift comes after U.S. backed negotiations failed to produce an agreement. Moscow continues to demand Ukrainian concessions, including territory in Donetsk, while Kyiv has rejected those terms. Expectations for upcoming U.S.- Russian diplomatic contacts are reportedly low. The escalation is occurring amid an expanding exchange of strikes. Ukraine has targeted Russian oil and logistics infrastructure, while Russia has continued attacks on Ukrainian energy and other infrastructure. Ukraine's limited supply of air-defense interceptors remains a concern. Source: https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-08-26/putin-moves-to-escalate-war-in-ukraine-with-talks-at-dead-end

headline: Overnight, a major flash flood struck the Nepal–Tibet border region, killing at least nine people and leaving hundreds missing. Video compiled by the BBC show the waters rapidly rising across the region. The flooding hit communities along the Lhende Khola River, sweeping away roads, bridges, homes and hydropower infrastructure. A massive mudslide also struck Gyirong Port, a major crossing between Nepal and Tibet, cutting roads, communications and power connections. Local authorities suspect an earthquake triggered an ice and rock avalanche into the river, producing the sudden surge of water. The scale of the incident is still unfolding. At least 348 people have been reported missing, including 105 Indians, 93 Nepalis, three Americans and 12 British nationals. Eight South Koreans working at a hydropower project are also missing. Authorities are warning that the danger may not be over. A blockage remains upstream on the Lhende Khola, raising the possibility of another major flood. Nepali and Chinese authorities are conducting rescue operations, with 574 Chinese rescuers deployed to the affected border crossing. India and South Korea are also coordinating assistance. Rescue helicopters have so far been unable to land in some areas because of the flooding and debris.
